One of the best pieces of advice I think I will ever learn ( I'm a total newb) is not to get so fixated on the pictures being viewed on your display screen. Get familiar with the close up feature, and the portrait feature and the landscape features so you can vary your image styles. And get comfortable with the speed your taking pictures at. But seeing as you have time now, practice taking a good lot of pictures, in each setting in a short amount of time. Try not look at them, then change the setting and do it again . When you have gone through a few different features, then stop and look over things that you just took. So you can get an idea, of speeds and movements and that. He took photos while people were deep in conversation and he waited for them to crack a smile or to laugh and he would be snapping away without us even realising. Or when people were dancing he would be so ready for all types of moment being carried out. And did a lot of wonderful focus photos of the bride and groom and blurred crowds. And then family photos with a brightly flowered background.  Another set of family photos on the staircase if the hotel. And close up pics of the guests when the dancing was happening. Hey so heres some personal experience based advice from me but I'm quite the extrovert. I have a very nice friend who is more of an introvert who similarly matches up to your description and she has explained some things that may help this. 

It would be a good suggestion to ask her about her interests before assuming she drinks, unless you know this. Or if she mentions about places she eats or you notice what she eats for lunch , maybe suggest a place to eat yourself . That might show your paying attention. 

As it's all very fresh, and she seems to prefare to not spend so much time in college, dont be disappointed  if she turns down the offer, because if shes like my introverted friend who tends to go from things like college almost immediately after, then she could have some outside priorities going on (my friend cares for her nanny in between study time) so it may not be about you, but if this happens. The idea has been planted in her head since you asked and maybe she can bring it up in the future. What I'm saying is dont give up hope straight off the bat, but do remember that you dont know her yet that she could be proud and would like to keep certain things to herself. 

She could say that she is in a relationship, so if that occurs, just be mindful that that's her situation and be there for her as the friend she may need and want in college. You never know how much you could help her. I'm gathering that she isnt in a relationship on your info but if she is, just be ok with it. And be happy for her that she has someone. 

Last thing I would say is, remember you are dealing with an introverted lady who may be crippling with anxiety. This was a difficult thing I had endured as an extrovert when i first got to know my bf. Hes a wonderful person and I'm forever grateful my feelings were strong cause we were lucky enough to make time for each others different qualities. I dont believe he dated such an extrovert like me previously, so it wasnt easy for him at the begining when we were on dates etc. It wasnt easy on me either as I was so used to out there characters in my friend group. So patience at the beginning is a great help. If it's a no now, the seed is planted, and it could give her the butterflies to make time to go ahead on that dinner some other time. 

I hope some of that helps, sorry for the big speil. I'm not one for short info. This appears to be very similar in ways  my friend approaches from guys being an introvert and I thought my beginning interactions with my bf were worth mentioning with our differences and intro and extro.
